item.1: The provider layout: the record, its widths and formats (the Zucchetti starter here is made up; their sample replaces it).
item.10: That a correction replaces the whole file (v2 replaces v1) rather than carrying only the differences.
item.11: The character set and line ends of the file.
item.12: How long our copy is kept (five years here).
item.2: The file format they import: fixed-width text, delimited text, or XML.
item.3: Their codes (voci, causali) for each hour type, absence code and earning type.
item.4: The company code (codice ditta) their software knows us by.
item.5: Decimal hours (7.50) rather than hours and minutes, and how negative amounts are written.
item.6: That night and holiday hours go as "of which" rows beside ordinary hours.
item.7: That agency and external people stay out of the file.
item.8: How a leaver's last working day is flagged.
item.9: That earnings of an earlier month go under their own code.
